name: JSON Formatter
summary: Parse valid JSON and serialize it with two-space indentation for readable browser-local inspection.
inputParameters: Valid JSON text accepted by JavaScript JSON.parse
useCases: Review compact API payloads
Normalize indentation before a code review

limitations: Invalid JSON is rejected rather than repaired.
Parsing and serialization follow JavaScript JSON semantics and can normalize number notation.
Processing occurs on the main browser thread and is limited by available memory.

name: JSON Minifier
summary: Parse valid JSON and remove insignificant formatting whitespace through compact serialization in the browser.
inputParameters: Valid JSON text accepted by JavaScript JSON.parse
outputFormats: Compact JSON text produced by JSON.stringify
useCases: Reduce JSON formatting overhead
Create a compact payload for copying into a request

limitations: Whitespace inside JSON string values is preserved.
Duplicate object keys are resolved by JSON.parse before serialization.
The engine does not calculate transfer compression such as gzip or Brotli.

name: Recursive JSON Key Sorter
summary: Sort object keys recursively with the browser locale comparator while preserving the order of array elements.
inputParameters: Valid JSON containing objects, arrays, or primitive values
outputFormats: Two-space-indented JSON with recursively sorted object keys
useCases: Make object-key order easier to compare
Prepare deterministic-looking JSON for human review

limitations: Key ordering uses String.localeCompare and can vary by runtime locale behavior.
Array element order is intentionally preserved.
The output is not a cryptographic canonical JSON format or signature-safe serialization.

name: HTML Entity Encoder
summary: Escape ampersands, angle brackets, double quotes, and apostrophes into common HTML entity forms.
inputParameters: Unicode text containing characters that may be significant in HTML
outputFormats: Plain text with five HTML-significant characters entity-encoded
useCases: Display a short HTML fragment as text
Prepare attribute-like text for manual inspection

limitations: Only ampersand, less-than, greater-than, double quote, and apostrophe are encoded.
Encoding text is not a complete context-aware XSS defense.
Safe output handling still depends on whether text enters HTML, attributes, URLs, CSS, or JavaScript contexts.

name: HTML Entity Decoder
summary: Decode six common named entities and valid decimal or hexadecimal numeric character references locally.
inputParameters: Text containing amp, lt, gt, quot, apos, nbsp, or numeric entities terminated by semicolons
outputFormats: Decoded Unicode text with unsupported entities preserved
useCases: Inspect entity-encoded snippets
Convert numeric character references into readable text

limitations: The named-entity table is intentionally limited and is not the complete HTML Living Standard table.
Entities without a terminating semicolon remain unchanged.
Decoding untrusted text does not make it safe to inject into HTML.

name: ASCII Text Slugifier
summary: Normalize a title into a lowercase ASCII slug with hyphen separators and a literal and replacement.
outputFormats: Lowercase ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens
useCases: Draft a human-readable URL path segment
Normalize simple English headings into identifiers

limitations: The engine removes characters that do not transliterate into ASCII letters or digits.
Ampersands become the word and, which may not match every editorial convention.
The result is not checked for route collisions, reserved words, or search keyword quality.

name: Exact Line Deduplicator
summary: Remove exact duplicate lines while preserving the first occurrence and normalizing line endings to line feeds.
inputParameters: Multiline text separated by LF, CRLF, or CR line endings
outputFormats: Deduplicated lines joined with LF characters
useCases: Remove repeated identifiers from a pasted list
Preserve first-seen ordering while cleaning exact duplicates

limitations: Comparison is exact and case-sensitive.
Leading and trailing whitespace is not trimmed before comparison.
Empty lines are treated as values and repeated empty lines collapse to the first occurrence.

name: Locale-Aware Line Sorter
summary: Sort normalized text lines with the browser runtime locale comparator and preserve duplicate line values.
inputParameters: Multiline text separated by LF, CRLF, or CR line endings
outputFormats: Sorted lines joined with LF characters
useCases: Alphabetize a short configuration list
Group similar human-readable values for review

limitations: Ordering uses localeCompare without an explicit locale or collation options.
Duplicate values are preserved.
The engine does not implement numeric, natural, case-insensitive, or reverse-sort modes.

name: URL Query String Parser
summary: Parse a raw query string or URL query section into JSON while preserving repeated parameter values as arrays.
inputParameters: Raw query text beginning optionally with question mark, or a URL containing a query section
outputFormats: Indented JSON object containing decoded parameter names and values
useCases: Inspect campaign query parameters
Review repeated API query keys before debugging a request

limitations: Parsing follows the browser URLSearchParams form-decoding behavior, including plus-to-space conversion.
Parameters without values become empty strings.
The engine does not validate that a full input URL is otherwise syntactically valid.

name: Unix and ISO Timestamp Converter
summary: Convert Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, or a parseable ISO date-time into normalized UTC representations.
inputParameters: Numeric Unix time or date-time text accepted by JavaScript Date.parse
outputFormats: JSON containing ISO, Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, and UTC text
useCases: Inspect an API epoch value
Normalize an ISO timestamp for debugging

limitations: Numeric magnitudes below one hundred billion are interpreted as seconds and larger values as milliseconds.
Fractional milliseconds are normalized by the JavaScript Date implementation.
Ambiguous non-ISO date strings can be parsed differently across runtimes and should be avoided.
